Senses.Explanation: The first graph means “alive”; the repeated fish graph depicts lively, darting movement: “alive and darting.” The literal fish wording remains visible in a verse about fine fish beneath the frozen Yellow River: they are “alive and darting, yet cannot leap out.” Chan records apply the expression to people, sayings, movement, stillness, and “this matter.” One hall address says, “In motion, constantly still; at rest, alive and darting,” and then says that motion and stillness are both forgotten. A case comment says that this matter “rolls and turns, alive and darting, like a pearl running on a tray, without a stagnant trace.” Blue Cliff Record requires an “alive and darting fellow” whose phrases and workings accord. Other records ask directly for “the alive-and-darting phrase” or place the expression beside “clean and naked, without turning back and forth.” These are the texts’ stated predicates and comparisons; the entry does not assign them an unstated inner quality.
Senses.Note: The headword occurs 229 times in 99 allowlisted texts. The common alternate spelling using the ordinary graph for lively occurs 175 times in 82 texts; the older Linji spelling with a different fish-side graph occurs 7 times in 4 texts. The adverbial form occurs 63 times in 37 texts. One text asks directly for the “alive-and-darting phrase.” The fish, person, phrase, and appraisal deployments share one descriptive expression rather than requiring separate senses.

Occurrences.Kwic: 動時常寂寂，靜處活鱍鱍。動靜兩俱忘，佛祖何處著。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: 續古尊宿語要, Jinsu Zhi section. Jinsu Zhi is the exact hall-verse speaker: he contrasts being constantly still while moving with being vividly alive in stillness, then says both movement and stillness are forgotten.

Occurrences.Kwic: 其實此事轉轆轆、活鱍鱍，如盤走珠，了無滯跡，方為可也。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Elder Linquan's Appraisals and Comments on Chan Master Danxia Zichun's Verses on Old Cases, the Empty Hall Collection (林泉老人評唱丹霞淳禪師頌古虗堂集), case seventeen. In the continuous commentary introduced by 師云, Linquan Conglun says that this matter turns freely and is alive and darting, like a pearl running on a tray without any stagnant trace. Dongshan Liangjie is the case subject invoked earlier in the comment, not the speaker of this sentence.

Occurrences.Kwic: 須是箇活鱍鱍漢。始得句句相投機機相應。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Blue Cliff Record of Chan Master Foguo Yuanwu (佛果圜悟禪師碧巖錄). In the pointer to case sixty-eight, Yuanwu Keqin says it must be an alive-and-darting fellow before phrase accords with phrase and dynamic responds to dynamic.

Occurrences.Kwic: 黃河凍已合，深處有嘉魚。活鱍鱍，跳不脫。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: 五燈全書(第34卷-第120卷). Complete Book of the Five Lamps (五燈全書), Meng'an Siyue section. Meng'an Siyue is the exact hall speaker who describes the fine fish beneath the frozen Yellow River as lively and splashing yet unable to leap free.
